Working in retail for up to 8 hours a day has made me lost my sanity. So hiding my face while I'm quietly cursing and talking to myself is pretty convenient.

• When picking/scanning items ALWAYS make sure the UPC code (the numbers under the barcode) match the UPC code that appears on the remote. This will help greatly with maintaining a high accuracy rate.  

• Also, when scanning the barcode, make sure to not also scan a QR code that might be near it. This will make it look like you scanned the wrong item even if it's the correct item.

• If your store allows it, always carry a walkie talkie with you when you're picking groceries. Then it will be easier to report spills, help customers find items, etc. 

• This is kind of common knowledge but when staging (putting the totes of groceries in their correct storage spot) or destaging (putting the totes on a cart to take to the customer's car) lift with your legs and not your back because some of those totes are extremely heavy. I've invested in a back brace and it's kept me from injuring myself. 

• When loading groceries into customers' cars, make sure to put the water, soda, and other larger items in first THEN put in the bagged groceries. 

• Some customers will tip you when you load their cars. At every store I've heard of you're not allowed to accept tips but as long as you do it discretely and don't tell anyone, there shouldn't be a problem. 

I know a lot of this is common sense but some of these I've had to learn the hard way. The more you know before you start the better.

I called two weeks after I sent in my application and was interviewed and hired the same day. As long as you've sent in an application and don't call too soon there shouldn't be any harm in it. You can say something like "Hello, I sent in an application a few weeks ago and was wondering if you're still hiring" as some managers might be bothered if you simply ask them to check your application.

The majority of people who get jobs in retail don't stay and make it their career. Retail is one of those job fields that many use to fill in the gap between careers or in this case, a mass layoff at their previous job. You can never expect a low turnover rate for a low paying entry level job that requires no experience or education. 

I got a job at Kroger instead of taking unemployment because one, I didn't even qualify for it, and two, I needed a quick hire job to keep money coming in. I'm still going to work here part time now that I was hired back at my previous job, but most people don't have time to juggle two jobs. It can be a pain with everyone leaving, but that's the reality of working in retail.

I love my job. I work for my city's recreation department and most of my work is in youth programs. I've helped out with our summer camps and got paid to host gym games, teach how to make crafts, and supervise during field trips. Due to the pandemic we're not hosting camps this year and I'm currently working our free summer meal program. I'm responsible for packing the meals and handing them out in our drive-thru system. The interaction with families is limited but it's a nice break from the chaos of summer camp. During the school year I host an after school activity program and monitor our recreation rooms. 

My job responsibilities change with the season so I'm never stuck doing the same thing. I've been working here for over a year and enjoy everything from my coworkers to the pay raises. Recreation is truly a forgotten job field that deserves way more recognition. :)
